guidance.procedure: Create a route table from each operative definition lead-in to every incorporated continuation before deciding any proposition. Technical-only scope is opposed when any route admits business, financial, commercial, customer, personnel, marketing, or other nontechnical material. Universal express identification holds only when every admission route requires the discloser to mark or expressly designate the material; automatic, contextual, reasonable-expectation, or nature-based coverage opposes it. Oral coverage requires an explicit oral, verbal, spoken, or visual route; generic disclosure language alone is insufficient. Cite every independently responsive route and any lead-in needed to supply its scope, but exclude headings and sibling branches that answer only another proposition.

Maintain separate disposition, retention, and survival ledgers. For disposition upon termination, first record the exact trigger: termination or expiration qualifies, while request, demand, completion, closing, or ended discussions alone does not. Retention requires an express archival, backup, compliance, dispute, professional-record, or inaccessible-copy exception; a return command alone is not permission, and an exhaustive all-materials-and-copies rule supports the opposed boundary. Survival requires confidentiality or use duties expressly continuing after termination, not agreement duration, ownership, disposition, or continuing confidentiality after return alone. Collect every responsive command, trigger, exception, and continuation before choosing spans, without transferring evidence between ledgers.

Analyze outsider disclosure, employee disclosure, and copying independently. For each disclosure rule, resolve any defined recipient class, then match actor, exact recipients, quantifier, modality, and attached need-to-know, purpose, authorization, and confidentiality conditions. Employee permission does not extend to consultants, agents, advisers, contractors, affiliates, or other outsiders; outsider permission does not automatically include employees. A general prohibition with only an employee exception opposes outsider permission, while silence or consent solely at the discloser's discretion settles neither. For copying, a necessity- or purpose-limited exception permits some copies, whereas an absolute or consent-only prohibition opposes permission; return of copies is not copying permission. Cite every independently operative rule and necessary recipient definition, excluding safeguards, liability, use limits, notice, and adjacent actions.

Reconstruct each exception as a complete chain: operative exclusion or permission lead-in, the responsive branch, and any attached conditions. Independent development requires development without using, referring to, relying on, accessing, or benefiting from protected information. Third-party acquisition requires an external source entitled to disclose and, when stated, free of a confidentiality obligation; prior possession, public availability, employee access, and independent development are separate branches. For compelled disclosure, separately verify legal compulsion, an actual notice duty or express excuse, protective-order opportunity, and any required-portion limitation. A heading, permission to obey law, or cooperation clause alone does not establish notice. Before answering, enumerate all fragments in the responsive chain and all independently operative notice provisions; exclude neighboring exception branches.

Search separately for each exact prohibited action, then complete its actor, protected object or people, duration, and operative exceptions. Reverse engineering requires an express ban on reverse engineering, decompiling, disassembling, decrypting, reconstructing, re-identifying, or materially equivalent analysis of protected material or an embodying product; copying, return, ownership, no-license, and general confidentiality are not substitutes. Representative solicitation requires recruiting, soliciting, inducing departure, hiring, employing, engaging, or comparable conduct directed at the specified people. Customer, vendor, transaction, competition, non-circumvention, and generic standstill restrictions are different objects. A matching prohibition supports the prohibitory proposition, an express permission opposes it, and absence is neutral. Cite each independently responsive prohibition and only conditions needed to complete it; headings and merely adjacent exceptions are not members.

Test recipient rights and agreement secrecy independently. No-right language includes an operative statement that no license, right, title, interest, option, or other right is granted or implied, and may also include explicit retained or exclusive ownership that leaves the recipient no proprietary right. Restricted use, access limits, a property heading, or a disclaimer without operative rights language is insufficient. Agreement secrecy requires protection of the agreement's existence or terms, or the fact, status, or substance of negotiations or discussions; ordinary confidentiality of disclosed information and entire-agreement clauses are not responsive. Collect every independently operative no-grant, retained-title, and responsive secrecy sentence, but exclude headings and neighboring use provisions.

Inventory every clause that operatively commits the receiving actor to use protected information only for a stated purpose or prohibits other use. Match actor, protected object, incorporated purpose, modality, and every exception or qualification. Include an introductory or recital-positioned sentence when it itself contains an operative commitment such as an agreement to disclose or receive solely for a purpose; exclude language that merely describes negotiations or motivation. Include a separate purpose definition only when an operative restriction incorporates it and the definition supplies the responsive purpose. A use-only or no-other-use rule supports the prohibitory proposition; broader express use permission opposes it, and silence settles neither. Cite all independently responsive repetitions and qualifications, excluding disclosure classes, copying, safeguards, ownership, no-license, remedies, and neighboring restrictions without a use condition.

delta.noop_reason: NOOP: The current paired observations do not support a new reusable source-selection boundary beyond the seven existing procedures. The principal failures—omitting definition lead-ins and incorporated branches, confusing disposition with retention, treating adjacent clauses as members, collapsing employee and outsider permissions, selecting unrelated solicitation or standstill provisions, and citing only one fragment of a complete exception or use chain—are already expressly covered. Current-memory performance also showed net harms in label accuracy, evidence F1, and joint exactness, with both missing members and extra citations; changing procedures or examples would therefore require an unsupported generalization rather than a source-backed repair.
